subject: chess
status: STAGED, not live. Owner approval needed (see curriculum-build/SKILL-CURRICULA.md, section 9).
doc: Novice-to-elite progression for the playing path C01-C13, with the professional (C14-C16) and frontier (C17-C19) tracks open alongside at any playing level. Each stage maps onto existing grades (ids from content/chess-grades.js) and says what the learner can DO at the end, how that is PROVED, how practice is built, how feedback is given and what the app senses. Gate numbers marked [R] are design values to be normed on real learners; no gate may be passed by self-report alone.

evidence_tags.V: page or text opened and read (this session or the subject's research files)
evidence_tags.P: from Savant's earlier research files (curriculum-build/chess/research/*.md), which carry their own sources
evidence_tags.L: computed by code in this folder (verify-skill-curricula.js)

charness2005.cite: Charness, Tuffiash, Krampe, Reingold & Vasyukova (2005): serious solo study the strongest predictor of rating; GMs ~5,000 h solo study in first decade

burgoyne2019.cite: Burgoyne et al. (2019), N=377: study+instruction+starting age explain 63% of peak-rating variance; tournament play adds R2 .006

gobet2007.cite: Gobet & Campitelli (2007): practice necessary not sufficient; 8x spread in practice needed to reach master

gobetsimon1996.cite: Gobet & Simon (1996) templates in chess memory

debruin2007.cite: de Bruin, Rikers & Schmidt (2007): predict + self-explain beat predict alone and observe for KR v K learners

bilalic2008.cite: Bilalic, McLeod & Gobet (2008) Einstellung: familiar non-optimal solution drops experts ~3 SD

rowland2014.cite: Rowland (2014) testing-effect meta-analysis: recall > recognition (0.61 v 0.29), feedback raises effect

chessable.cite: Chessable MoveTrainer intervals 4h,1d,3d,1w,2w,1mo,3mo,6mo; a timer per move (support.chess.com/en/articles/10319322)

act2005.cite: van der Maas & Wagenmakers (2005) A psychometric analysis of chess expertise, Am J Psychol 118(1): the Amsterdam Chess Test (choose-a-move, predict-a-move, recall, verbal knowledge); reliable, high predictive validity against Elo; response times add validity on easy items. https://dare.uva.nl/id/44227bd6-730b-4f8d-885d-6c7d08d1eebf

regan2011.cite: Regan & Haworth (2011) Intrinsic Performance Ratings: move quality over many moves tracks Elo

kalyuga2005.cite: Kalyuga & Sweller (2005) Rapid dynamic assessment of expertise to improve the efficiency of adaptive e-learning, ETR&D 53, 83-93 (first-step / rapid verification diagnosis of expertise)

tetzlaff2025.cite: Tetzlaff et al. (2025) expertise reversal meta-analysis (60 experiments), as used in docs/SCORECARD.md 'Reach'

guadagnoli2004.cite: Guadagnoli & Lee (2004) Challenge point framework, J Motor Behav 36(2) 212-224: the optimal difficulty depends on the learner's skill (functional vs nominal difficulty)

lichessdata.cite: 1500-1700 Lichess players: more daily games inversely related to rating gain (emerginginvestigators.org/articles/25-024); puzzle ratings run above game ratings

pert.cite: Pert's error lists by band 1600-2000 (curriculum-build/chess/research/03 section 3)

steps.cite: Steps Method: mating postponed until play is fluent (chess.co.uk Step 1)

tables.cite: Our own retrograde tables (lib/endgame-tables.js): KQK max distance-to-mate 10, KRK 16, every white-to-move position won; KPK win/draw for every position

competence_model.doc: What a chess learner IS, as the app tracks it. Each component has its own evidence and its own gate; none stands in for another.

components.what: Legal moves and rules without hesitation
components.evidence: board answers (tap/drag), timed; chess_moves, chess_board items

components.what: Tactical motifs, mating patterns, endgame positions recognised fast
components.evidence: Glicko-2 puzzle rating per theme family with RD (content/chess-trainer.js); per-move SRS cards (content/chess-srs.js)

components.what: Forcing lines seen to the end, opponent replies included
components.evidence: multi-move puzzles where every learner move is graded; visualisation drills (pieces hidden)

components.what: Finding that a tactic exists (or does not) in unlabelled positions; the move-checking habit
components.evidence: unannounced positions with 'nothing works' items; blunder rate in own games

components.what: Winning won endings and holding drawn ones against best defence
components.evidence: play-outs against perfect defence (tables), scored against distance to mate

components.what: Evaluation and plans in quiet positions
components.evidence: choose-a-move items accepted within an engine threshold plus a reason; guess-the-move through annotated games

components.what: Results and move quality in real games
components.evidence: rapid games against calibrated bots (Maia-2 bands where installed): performance rating with its standard error, blunder count by win-probability loss

components.what: Rules details, notation, history, professional knowledge

gate_rules.proof_only: A stage, unit or lesson is skipped or passed only on measured evidence: board answers, rated puzzles, play-outs and games. Self-report, time spent and the after-level model read never prove anything (same rule as GAP-PATHS-SPEC 'nothing may be marked known without evidence').
gate_rules.cold: Performance gates count only cold attempts: the first attempt of a day, at least 20 hours after the skill was last practised (retention, not warm-up performance; research/02 section 7).
gate_rules.two_days: Every performance gate needs passes on two different days.
gate_rules.unannounced: Tactics gates are sat in unannounced mode (no theme given; some positions have nothing) because themed puzzles inflate success (lichessdata).
gate_rules.rating_with_uncertainty: A rating gate needs rating >= target AND RD <= 80 (about +/-160 at 95%).
gate_rules.game_gate_size: A game-performance gate needs at least 12 rated rapid games: the standard error of a performance rating over n games near a 50% score is about 347/sqrt(n) Elo (L: 100 Elo at 12 games), so games are only one of several signals and never the only one.
gate_rules.unit_belief: Knowledge units use the live learnerPath.unitBelief (services/learner-path.js, current knobs HOLE_PRIOR 0.15, ISLAND_PRIOR 0.65, SLIP 0.15, LUCK 0.15, KNOWN_AT 0.965). A board answer is graded as one of ~30 legal moves, so its guess rate is far lower than 4-option multiple choice and fewer right answers prove a unit (L, computed with the live function: 2 right board answers v 3 multiple-choice for a 'past' unit; 2 v 4 for an 'island' unit). Board-answer unit banks therefore make placement and test-outs shorter for the same safety.
gate_rules.norming: Thresholds marked [R] are provisional. After 200 learners have sat a stage's battery, cuts are re-set from the data (the score separating learners who then pass the next stage's game gate from those who do not), and the change is logged.

stages.name: Board explorer
stages.who: Never seen a board; age 4+ (voice-led) or an adult on day one
objectives: Moves each piece legally from any square, including blocked lines and the pawn's move-versus-capture asymmetry
Captures and protects in mini-games (pawn wars, capture-the-pawns) without moving into danger more than rarely
Sets up the starting position from memory with the light square on the right

exit.knowledge: C01 units proved by board answers (unit_belief)

performance.test: tap every square a piece can reach, 6 pieces x 3 random positions
performance.threshold: >= 95% squares right, no illegal square tapped twice

performance.test: collect-the-stars mazes for rook, bishop, queen, knight within the move par
performance.threshold: 3 of 4 pieces at par on a cold day

performance.test: place all 32 pieces

practice.games: mini-games only; no full games yet (Steps method)

feedback: Immediate, voice-led, show the legal squares after any wrong tap
Stars against a move par (Lichess Learn pattern)
sensing: voice prompts out; no camera or mic needed

stages.name: Rules learner
stages.who: Plays a full legal game; online 100-400
objectives: Plays a complete legal game: check, three ways out of check, castling conditions, promotion, en passant, draw rules
Tells checkmate from stalemate and check on sight
Finds mate in one in unlabelled positions
Mates with K+Q v K and two rooks against perfect defence

exit.knowledge: C02 units proved (rules items are computed by content/chess-board.js; perft-checked)

performance.test: 20 mixed positions: check, mate, stalemate or none
15 positions, mate in one present in 10, absent in 5 ('no mate' is an answer)
5 random won K+Q v K starts against perfect defence (tables)
performance.threshold: mate in every start within DTM+6 moves and never stalemate

performance.test: 2 full games against the lowest bot
performance.threshold: no illegal-move attempt that the learner did not correct, game recorded

practice.difficulty_target: 70-85% first-try success on puzzles (expected score 0.75: puzzle rating about 190 below the learner's)
practice.games: untimed or 15+10 against a friendly bot

feedback: Immediate on puzzles, with the refutation of a wrong move played on the board
Stalemate warning replayed when it happens in a play-out

stages.name: Beginner tactician
objectives: Runs the checks-captures-threats scan for both sides before every move
Wins hanging pieces and stops hanging own pieces
Recognises forks, pins, skewers, discovered attacks and removing the defender
Mates with K+R v K against perfect defence; wins simple pawn races

performance.test: fixed-form set of 30 positions rated about 600-1000 on our puzzle scale, mixed motifs, 5 with no tactic
5 random won K+R v K starts against perfect defence
performance.threshold: mate in all within DTM+8, no stalemate, within the 50-move rule

performance.test: 12 rapid games (15+10) against the 600-800 bot band
performance.threshold: median <= 1 piece left en prise per game AND score >= 40%

exit.retention: Tactics set repeated with new positions after 7+ days

practice.games: 10-15 minute games; blitz is a labelled fun mode, not practice

feedback: Puzzles immediate; games delayed: learner marks their 'oops' and 'best' moves before any engine view
Each own blunder becomes a 'find the better move' card on the SRS queue

stages.name: Novice club player
objectives: Uses double check, overloading, trapped pieces, x-ray and desperado in combinations
Knows opposition, the square of the pawn and K+P v K wins and draws
Plays one opening system per colour from principles, with its plans
Annotates own slow games before the engine

performance.test: 30 positions about 900-1300 on our scale, 6 with nothing
20 K+P v K positions: win or draw with the side to move
4 won K+P v K positions against perfect defence; 2 drawn positions defended as Black
12 rapid games against the 900-1100 bot band
performance.threshold: score >= 50% with median blunders (win-probability loss >= 0.20) <= 1 per game

feedback: Hint ladder on puzzles (theme, then piece, then square) costs stars
Game review: learner's annotations first, then the coach names the pattern from the curriculum

stages.name: Club player
objectives: Calculates forcing lines 3-4 moves deep including the opponent's best replies
Uses deflection, decoy, interference and clearance; re-checks the final position of a line
Plays key squares and basic rook endings; converts extra material
Recognises weak pawns, holes and outposts and makes a plan from them

performance.test: rated puzzles in unannounced mode
performance.threshold: rating at or above the stage cut with RD <= 80 (provisional cut: 80% success on a 30-item set at 1200-1500)

performance.test: 10 positions where the full line (3+ learner moves, every reply) must be entered
12 rapid games against the 1200-1400 band (Maia-2 1200-1400 where installed)

exit.retention: Repeat a parallel calculation set after 7+ days

practice.difficulty_target: 70-85% on single-move sets; about 60% on full-line calculation (challenge point rises with skill)
practice.games: 15+10 or slower, at most about 3 a day (anti-volume)

feedback: Wrong calculation shows the refutation line move by move
Every game reviewed: 3 critical moments marked by the learner first

stages.name: Intermediate
objectives: Lists candidate moves before calculating; defends against the opponent's tactics
Plays Lucena and Philidor, queen v pawn, wrong-bishop and fortress draws
Knows zugzwang and uses it in pawn endings
Simplifies when ahead

performance.test: unannounced rated puzzles incl. defensive positions
Lucena win and Philidor hold against an engine/tablebase
12 rapid games, 1400-1600 band

practice.session_minutes: 30-60, with 2-4 deep sessions a week of 45-90 min (a slow game plus analysis)

feedback: Defensive puzzles: a wrong move shows the opponent's winning reply
Endgame play-outs scored against the best result, not the engine number
sensing: engine (server, Stockfish/Leorik) for review where installed

stages.name: Strong club player
objectives: Calculates 4+ move lines and compares candidates by their final positions; blunder-checks the quiet move
Uses a repertoire learned as plans first, then drilled on the move trainer
Plays IQP and hanging-pawn structures, minority attacks, triangulation, K+B+N v K
Attacks the castled king when the conditions are met (Greek gift)

performance.test: unannounced rated puzzles
move-trainer cards for own repertoire
performance.threshold: >= 90% of due cards right on first try over 2 weeks, every card has its reason

performance.test: 12 rapid/classical games, 1600-1800 band (Maia-2 where installed)

exit.retention: SRS continues; endgame and structure checks after 14+ days

feedback: Repertoire: a deviation shows the plan, not only the move

stages.name: Advanced club player
objectives: Prophylaxis: names the opponent's plan before choosing a move
Converts advantages and decides exchanges well
Rook-ending theory (Vancura, short side) and corresponding squares
Manages the clock under pressure

performance.test: ACT-style choose-a-move set (tactical, positional, endgame thirds), timed
performance.threshold: stage cut [R], accepted within an engine threshold of 0.3 pawns plus the stated reason

performance.test: 5 '+3' positions converted and 3 worse positions held against an engine
12 games, 1800-2000 band

feedback: Annotation first; the engine is a check on the learner's analysis, not a substitute

stages.name: Expert
objectives: Deeper calculation (5 plies blind), opponent's candidates, repertoire with model games, Einstellung checks

performance.test: ACT-style set at expert level

Maia-2 tops out at its 2000+ band, so games against it cannot certify 2000+; use the strongest engine level calibrated against Maia-2 2000+ plus an imported FIDE/national/online rating as a discounted prior
performance.threshold: performance >= 2000 on the calibrated scale OR an external rating >= 2000 with RD/k-factor known

performance.test: Intrinsic-performance-style estimate from 20+ of the learner's own slow games (engine move quality, server side)
performance.threshold: shown as an estimate with its error; not a gate on its own

feedback: Exercises built from the learner's own critical positions (Dvoretsky style), multi-solution, graded by engine threshold

stages.name: Master to elite (taught as understanding and doing what such players do)
objectives: The tasks those players face: preparing for a named opponent, converting a technical ending at their level, calculating long forcing lines, building and maintaining a repertoire with engines

performance.test: capstone tasks graded against engine analysis and a rubric (preparation file, annotated game, technical conversion)
FIDE or national rating import

stages.honesty: The app does not certify a title or a 2200+ rating; no bot it has is a calibrated 2400 opponent. These grades say 'you can do what players at this level do', measured by tasks.

tracks_any_level.doc: Knowledge tracks (coaching, arbiting, problems, history, engines, theory). Gated by unit_belief on items plus applied tasks; open at any playing level, except that solving/composition and engine-research grades recommend (never force) CH6+ tactics for comprehension.

practice_engine.puzzle_selection: Pick puzzles with expected score 0.75 for the learner: puzzle rating = learner rating - 400*log10(0.75/0.25) = learner rating - 191 (L). For calculation sets from CH4 on, expected score 0.6 (rating - 70).
practice_engine.interleaving: A motif is practised blocked inside its lesson, then appears only in mixed, unannounced sets from the next lesson on (research/02 section 7; interleaving helps most for similar-looking categories).
practice_engine.variation: Every motif is met in 3+ board locations, both colours and mirrored (chunks are location-specific; gobetsimon1996).
practice_engine.srs: One per-move queue (content/chess-srs.js) for mating patterns, endgame technique, own-game mistakes and, from CH6, repertoire. A 'why' is shown before each new opening move (understanding before memorising).
practice_engine.own_games: From CH2: every rated game gets the learner's own annotation of 3 critical moments before any engine view; each mistake (win-probability loss >= 0.10) becomes a 'find the better move' SRS card.
practice_engine.anti_volume: Learning games are 15+10 or slower; more than about 3 games a day without review gets a nudge to review instead (lichessdata). Blitz is a labelled fun mode.

adaptation.doc: How each learner's path changes. Every lever changes HOW and HOW MUCH is practised; none removes an objective that is not proved.

levers.rule: Subject placement plus an in-grade unit placement on board answers; skill batteries (tactics set, a play-out, an optional bot game, an optional imported rating as a discounted prior) set the starting stage. Units before the placed one are 'past' (prior 0.85); a unit is known only by unit_belief.

Each lesson opens with one independent item and one transfer item (the first-step check). Both right on the first try, cold, moves the lesson to 'provisional'; it becomes 'known' only after a cold spaced check 1+ day later. One miss: the full worked -> faded -> independent ladder runs.

Worked and faded examples (A1-A2) shrink when the scorecard's per-subject reach is high (items well within reach) and grow when it is low; A4 stops early once two clean solves are followed by a clean transfer item.
Puzzle ratings chosen for expected score 0.75 (0.6 for calculation); after 3 misses in a row the next item is 150 points easier; frustration directive from the scorecard lowers it further.
Theme families whose per-theme rating is 150+ below the overall rating get 2x the share of the mixed sets until the gap closes; never more than half of a set, so interleaving survives.
Per-move SRS intervals; when the forgetting model is fitted (20+ learners), review when predicted recall < 85% (SCORECARD.md 'review-pick=model').
Own-game errors are tagged by curriculum pattern; a pattern missed in 2+ games re-opens its lesson's practice items (not the whole grade).
Learner chooses opening repertoire (from the curriculum's systems), bot personality, session length and kid/adult voice; choices never change gate content.
Ages 4-7: voice-led, 5-15 min sessions, mate postponed to C02, no clocks; the scorecard's attention-runway and fatigue stats shorten sessions further when confident.

never: Never skip a unit without unit_belief proof or a passed stage battery
Never pass a performance gate on warm (same-session) attempts only
Never certify a rating or title; show ratings with their uncertainty
Never let a themed-puzzle success rate stand in for unannounced success

needs_from_other_builds.from: chess engine / puzzles agent (services/chess-engine.js, content/chess-trainer.js, chess-srs.js)
needs_from_other_builds.need: per-theme Glicko sub-ratings; an 'unannounced' trainer mode that mixes in no-tactic positions (verified by engine: no move gains >= 1.5 pawns); a play-out mode against our KQK/KRK/KPK tables (staged here in lib/endgame-tables.js) and later 5-man tablebases; a 'performance rating with SE' for bot games
bands 1100-2000 used as calibrated opponents for CH4-CH7 game gates; below 1000 the app bot
